items.title: The State of Tabular AI Report 2026: What's exciting in Tabular AI right now?
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>Tabular AI,  the subset of AI concerned with grounding decisions on tabular data, is moving faster than ever. Agents now build machine learning pipelines in seconds, TFMs are opening new ways to predict, and scikit-learn was downloaded almost 2.3 billion times in the past year alone.

But no single team drives this progress. It comes from maintainers, researchers, and labs around the world, building in the open and on each other's work.

In the State of Tabular AI Report 2026, we brought together 50+ experts to share their perspectives and bets for 2027. In this video, Gaël Varoquaux and Cailean Osborne, authors of the report, and Madelon Hulsebos, author of the foreword, share what excites them most👇

items.title: The State of Tabular AI Report is out now!
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>📊 Tabular AI,  the subset of AI concerned with grounding decisions on tabular data, is moving faster than ever. Agents now build #machinelearning pipelines in seconds and #TFMs are opening new ways to predict. 

For enterprises, that means faster models behind everyday decisions: who gets credit, when demand will peak, which machine needs repair next.

But this speed raises new questions: where is the value, which models can you actually use, and how do you know they hold up? 

That's why our CSO, Gaël Varoquaux, and our Head of Ecosystem Development, Cailean Osborne, wrote this report. It maps where Tabular AI stands today, the innovations shaping it, and the people driving them.

What you can expect:

📈 The enterprise opportunity: Generative AI may dominate the headlines, but industry research indicates that Tabular AI dominates the P&L.

🔧 scikit-learn: The Swiss Army knife of machine learning keeps growing, with 2.3 billion downloads in the past year alone. Learn about the roadmap priorities.

⚒️ The Python data science ecosystem: The foundational tools of Tabular AI sustained by global communities committed to keeping them open and free.

🚀 Tabular foundation models: A fast-moving frontier of Tabular AI propelled by a culture of open science shared among the leading labs.

🤖 Agentic data science: How agents accelerate workflows and shift the bottleneck from pipeline building to validating agent-driven experiments.

Thank you to Madelon Hulsebos for the foreword, and to the leaders and open source developers from NVIDIA, IBM, Soda - Inria, Prior Labs, SAP, Fundamental, Intel, Quansight, QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, PyMC Labs and Probabl, among others, who shared their perspectives in the report.

🎤 Want to discuss it further? Gaël, Cailean and Madelon will host a webinar on December 2nd to talk about the main insights of the report.
